rationale: Neither a stepped-wedge trial nor a before-after chart review is the right first step. Prompts increase documentation (c1), but whether the notes reflect real conversations is contested (c3), templates alone can produce tick-box notes (c2), and the outcomes a trial would rely on have not been tested here: quality rating needs calibration (c4) and family response is low (c5). A six-month feasibility study on two wards tests delivery, measurement and recruitment against pre-specified progression criteria before six wards are committed to a trial.
alternatives: Stepped-wedge randomised trial across six wards now (deferred: outcomes untested and the evidence on quality conflicts)
Before-after chart review of documentation rates (refused: would count tick-box notes as success)
Implement the template without evaluation (refused: the hospital cannot tell whether conversations improve)
guidelines: CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility studies (adapted for a non-randomised feasibility study)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial now would spend the hospital's one release window and the grant on outcomes that may not be measurable; the feasibility study answers that at a fraction of the cost.

decision.statement: Before any stepped-wedge trial, run a six-month feasibility study on two wards that tests delivery of the template, prompts and skills session, the reliability of a calibrated quality score and the response of bereaved families, with progression criteria set in advance.
decision.question: What should the hospital do first to evaluate the serious illness conversation template?

criteria.text: Prompts increased documentation in a randomised trial, so a later trial could be worthwhile.
Whether templates improve the quality of documented conversations is uncertain, so the quality measure must be tested before a trial.
The quality score cannot reach kappa of 0.6 with local raters after calibration.

gates.requirement: Template scheduled in a record build release
gates.evidence: Change request CR-2026-3341 for the February 2027 release, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Protected nurse practitioner time for the evaluation
gates.evidence: Program director approval PC-2026-19, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Release of ward staff on two wards for the skills session
gates.evidence: Nursing director agreement DIV-NUR-2026-44 dated 2026-09-11, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Chart review of documentation rates only
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c3, c4 and c5 from retrieved records, including c3, which carries high uncertainty because the evidence conflicts; that uncertainty is the reason for the feasibility step.

summary: Feasibility study first; the decision rests on four ledger claims, one of them highly uncertain, and all gates are met.
